title: EmberLynx reserved GPU ops and burst requirements
summary: Initial discovery with EmberLynx to map reserved GPU needs and failure/fallback patterns. Key concerns: strict isolation for PII workloads, predictable burst capacity during model rollouts, and procurement timelines for Dedicated vs Private. Redwood to provide pricing/benchmark artifacts and a tailored POC proposal.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-06-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO EmberLynx), Liam (Head Infra), Sara (ML Eng), Tom (Procurement)

Summary / Notes (auto): discussed Dedicated reserved GPU options, isolation requirements, burst/hotpool patterns, security controls. Redwood to follow up with pricing and benchmark sims.

[00:00] Evan: All right thanks everyone for jumping on, uh this is Evan from Redwood inference, I'm the account lead. We got Priya from our SE team as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: Good thanks, Maya here. Thanks for making time, we've been trying to lock down a plan for dedicated capacity for our inference workloads.
[00:18] Liam: Hey all, Liam. We want to understand the isolation bit and how burst works - especially around prewarm and eviction behavior.
[00:25] Priya: Hi folks, Priya. Quick agenda — we'll run through your current profile, talk about Dedicated vs Private considerations, isolation patterns, burst/hotpool strategies, and next steps for a POC scope. Sound ok?
[00:36] Sara: Yep, that's perfect. I'll be mostly on the perf numbers and our service level constraints.
[00:40] Tom: And I'll stick around for procurement questions.

-- Discovery / context --
[01:05] Evan: Maya, can you give us a little background on the workload — model sizes, typical seq lengths, qps, any PII/residency constraints?
[01:15] Maya: Sure. So we run two main models for customer chat and document extraction. The chat model is a 13B open model, avg seq ~512 tokens but peaks to 2k on longer docs. Doc extraction uses a 7B with heavy context windows. Our avg qps per service is around 800–1.2k, spiking to 2k during new release traffic, and we target p95 generation latency under 250ms for chat. We also have regulated customers where data must remain in our VPC.
[01:45] Evan: Great, that helps. So sounds like you need predictable throughput with occasional high spikes — a classic reserved+burst pattern.
[01:52] Liam: Exactly. We can't have noisy neighbors affecting PII processing. Isolation is a must. We were considering either Dedicated (Redwood managed reserved GPU pool) or Private (customer VPC/on-prem). Cost is a factor so we want a tradeoff.
[02:06] Priya: Quick note on isolation patterns: Dedicated can provide tenant-level isolation via node reservation and tenancy fencing. For stricter compliance, Private gives you full control of VPC and KMS integration. Many customers pick Dedicated for predictable throughput with strict guardrails and then Private if they need fully air-gapped or HIPAA-level isolation.

-- Mis-transcription / clarification --
[03:00] Speaker 1: Did you say KV cache or K-V cash?
[03:03] Priya: It's K-V cache, sorry speech system sometimes hyphens. We use prefix and KV cache to avoid re-computation and that reduces cost for repeated contexts.

-- Burst strategy discussion --
[03:35] Liam: Walk us through how bursts are handled. We have daily spikes, and occasional insane spikes with marketing events. We need a plan for prewarm or hot-pools.
[03:46] Priya: Sure. There are a few levers: reserved baseline capacity (what you commit to), a warm/hot pool for fast scale ups, and on-demand burst to hosted capacity as a fallback. For Dedicated we offer a warm pool add-on which pre-warms a set of nodes — they are sticky to your tenant for X minutes to reduce cold starts. You can also configure burst routing policy so non-sensitive traffic can fall back to Redwood Hosted if you've okayed that.
[04:15] Sara: How sticky is sticky? Like will a user's session hit the same prewarmed KV cache?
[04:20] Priya: Sticky in the sense of warm warm nodes staying resident; session-level stickiness isn't guaranteed unless you deploy session routing in your application. The KV cache is managed per model instance; if requests hit a prewarmed instance you'll benefit from cache. There is some nuance with eviction policies — if your hotpool is full and we preempt LRU, you'll see cold starts on next request.
[04:40] Evan: Also, for extremely sensitive tenants, we can pin models to isolated nodes so no multi-tenancy. That increases cost but gives strict tenant fencing.

-- Security/compliance --
[05:10] Maya: We need SOC2, SSO, KMS encryption and audit logs. Does Dedicated include customer-managed KMS?
[05:18] Evan: Dedicated supports integrations with customer KMS for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can provide tenant-level encryption keys and centralized audit logs. We have SOC2 docs and granular trace logs. We'll share the SOC2 cert and our KMS integration notes after the call.
[05:33] Liam: What about data-at-rest on GPUs? Are they wiped between tenants?
[05:38] Priya: Yes — disks and NVMe ephemeral storage are wiped on deprovision and GPUs don't persist data; we also scrub KV caches on handoff. For Private/on-prem you control the hardware lifecycle.

-- Cost / pricing concerns --
[06:05] Tom: From procurement side, we need rough numbers. Are burst hours billed differently? What's the billing cadence for Dedicated reserved nodes?
[06:14] Evan: Reserved nodes are committed monthly or annually — we have tiers. Warm pool and burst add-ons are priced by node-hour and by the maximum throughput you enable. Burst fallback to Hosted is billed at normal hosted rates and metered per-token during fallbacks. We'll send a clear worksheet.
[06:32] Tom: Ok, will need this for our finance review.

-- Technical deep-dive moments --
[07:10] Sara: We use 4 KB and 16 KB token batches in different flows; batching behavior matters. Does Redwood support workload-aware batching and compile-time kernel selection?
[07:22] Priya: Yes, runtime picks kernels based on model arch and sequence profiles. We do continuous batching and can prioritize latency SLOs. For your mixed batch sizes we'll recommend per-route configs. That's part of the POC work.
[07:38] Sara: Great, can we test scenario with our typical payloads?
[07:41] Priya: Absolutely, that's what the POC sim is for. We'll also include a KV/cache hit-rate forecast.

-- Failure and fallback patterns --
[08:05] Liam: If Dedicated capacity saturates, what's the behavior? Do requests queue? Do they drop? Does Redwood auto-fallback?
[08:14] Priya: You can configure routing rules. Options: queue until capacity frees (within SLO), reject with a clear error, or fallback to another model variant or to Hosted. We advise a hybrid: route non-sensitive traffic to Hosted as fallback, keep sensitive traffic queued or reject to preserve privacy. We'll show you sample policies.
[08:35] Maya: Queueing is risky for user experience; we might prefer graceful degradation — shorter responses or reranking.
[08:42] Evan: Exactly — that's a common approach: degrade quality for a subset during storms. Priya will sketch possible fallback policies in the POC doc.

-- Questions from EmberLynx --
[09:10] Sara: Any limits on number of hotpool nodes?
[09:13] Priya: Not operationally, but there's an economy of scale. Prewarming too many nodes is costly. We'll model cost curves.
[09:22] Liam: How fast can we scale from cold to warm? Minutes? Tens of seconds?
[09:27] Priya: With prewarm pool live, cold starts are usually < 10s; exact depends on model size and quantization. For fully warm nodes it's essentially immediate for new requests.

-- Noise / transcription glitches --
[10:00] Speaker 2: (laughs) the thing about the red-wood, wood?
[10:03] Evan: Redwood, yes. :)

-- Procurement and timelines --
[11:12] Tom: If we want Dedicated, what typical lead time? We need contract by end of month ideally.
[11:19] Evan: For standard configs we can do a 30–45 day onramp for Dedicated sizing and SLAs. Shorter if you accept standard configs; Private/on-prem will take longer. For a pilot we can start sooner with Hosted-backed Dedicated POC.
[11:34] Tom: Ok we'll align internal approval windows.

-- Recap and commitments --
[12:05] Evan: To recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2 + KMS brief, Priya will run the performance sim and baseline latency vs cost doc, and you will send traffic profiles and infra diagrams. We'll then schedule a POC scoping call.
[12:20] Maya: Sounds good. One more ask: will you provide a sample SLO contract wording for the Dedicated SLA?
[12:28] Evan: Yes we'll include an SLO draft in the SOW.

-- Closing --
[12:45] Liam: Thanks folks, this was useful. We'll follow up with files.
[12:50] Priya: Thanks everyone, Evan I'll capture the action items and send calendar invite for the POC scoping.
[12:58] Tom: Appreciate it. Bye.

Notes: transcription contains some auto-attribution noise (Speaker 1/2) and occasional mis-heard tech terms. Action items captured above.
